elements.element: Customer is not subject to any employee non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly binds both parties: “Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party.” Customer therefore remains subject to a non-solicitation restriction.

elements.element: The employee non-solicitation restriction is mutual.
elements.evidence: “Neither party” imposes the same restriction on Customer and the other party.

elements.element: The restriction applies only to personnel directly involved in the performance or receipt of the Services.
elements.evidence: The second sentence expressly limits the restriction to “employees directly involved in the performance or receipt of the Services.”

elements.element: The restricted period is tied to each covered employee’s involvement and ends 12 months after that involvement ends.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the restriction applies “for 12 months from the end of their involvement.” The preceding word “during” lacks an express object, but the employee-specific end trigger and 12-month period are stated.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that it “does not restrict general advertisements.”

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by personnel are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly excludes “unsolicited approaches by an employee of the other party.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring personnel who were not solicited.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition addresses solicitation only; it contains no prohibition on hiring or employing personnel.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains bound. It substantively achieves every fallback element: mutuality, service-involved personnel scope, an employee-specific 12-month tail, both required carve-outs, and no no-hire restriction. The revision is confined to the solicitation provision and preserves unrelated terms. Drafting quality is reduced by the incomplete phrase “during and for 12 months,” which should read “during their involvement and for 12 months after the end of their involvement,” although the required duration and trigger remain discernible.
